title: headwater-database-import/1
description: What `headwater database import-excel --json` and `headwater database import-brightway --json` print: where the database was written, what became of each line, and what validation found. Example: `headwater database import-excel tshirt.xlsx --release toy-background@6864b7dbb65d --out project/tshirt-excel --json`.

name.description: The name of the database written, the prefix of its process ids.

replaced.description: The folder held the unedited files of an earlier import, and they were replaced.

clean.description: Every line mapped, every formula and parameter copied, and a database that validates and that `calc` will not refuse.

source.description: For import-excel, the workbook's file name. For import-brightway, the name of the project's folder.

source_database.description: The source's own name for its database, as Brightway names it.

release.description: The release linked to, `name@hash` with the first 12 characters of the hash.

lines.description: The number of exchange rows of each status.

mapped_by.description: How the mapped lines were linked: the number of lines for each code, such as `release` or `reference`.

to_decide.description: Every line that is not mapped, and every mapped line linked by name only.

skipped_activities.description: One per activity that was not converted, with the reason.

databases.description: Each database the source's lines name, and what the import took it for.

uses.description: The other databases this database uses.

unused_mapping.description: Rows of the mapping file that no line needed.

notes.description: Things a person should know that are not failures: a formula that disagrees with the number next to it, a column that was not read, a skipped sheet.

validation.description: What validation of the written database found. Null when it did not run.

validation_skipped.description: Why validation did not run. Null when it ran.

method_folders.description: Method folders given with --method whose method the release does not hold. validate, calc and diff need them as --method-folder.

line.description: The row as a person finds it in the sheet: `name | reference product | location`.

status.description: mapped: written with its supplier or flow. unmapped: could not be linked, written with no supplier. waiting: buys from another database whose folder is not there yet. unexpressible: linked, but its formula is not in headwater's syntax.

suggestions.description: Processes or flows a person might have meant. Only to read, never applied.

database.description: For a `waiting` line: the database folder it will buy from.

by_name.description: For a line linked with no reference product or no location, because exactly one process fits: the supplier, and what the workbook left out. Accepted, and listed to be reviewed.

line_id.description: The line this row became in the database, when it was written.

item.description: What is wrong, for example `tshirt:tshirt line e02` or `flow toy:n2o`.

location.description: A file and a row, when known.

text.description: The line `validate` prints for this problem.
